title: Gilgamesh Tablet XI — The Flood Narrative: Utnapishtim recounts the deluge to Gilgamesh

translation.sourceText: Standard Babylonian Akkadian reconstruction from named scholarly editions (George 2003 critical edition; Thompson 1930 PD; Smith 1873 PD; Foster 2005 Before the Muses 3rd ed.)
translation.sourceLicense: Best-effort reconstruction; scholarly editions cited as references; English original to this project
translation.sourceAccessedVia: Foster 2005 + George 2003 + Thompson 1930 PD + Heidel 1946 + Tigay 1982
translation.verificationStatus: best-effort reconstruction; verification pending against George 2003 critical edition + original Nineveh codicology (BM K series)

editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.issue: Standing-epithet *rūqu* of Utnapishtim — rendered 'the Distant' (Foster 2005) vs. 'the Faraway' (George 2003) vs. 'the Far-Distant' (Kovacs); both translate the same lexeme but commit slightly different connotations (spatial-cosmographic vs. temporal-archaic).
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.default_taken: the Distant (Foster 2005)

editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.issue: *balāṭa teššēʾi* 'you sought (eternal) life' — the noun *balāṭu* here carries the technical sense of *immortality* but the lexeme is the same as ordinary 'life'. Whether to render 'eternal life' (interpretive-glosss) or 'life' (literal) is a recurring decision-point across the tablet.
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.default_taken: (eternal) life with the parenthetical bracket — preserves the literal Akkadian while signalling the technical semantic-field

editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.issue: *amāt niṣirti* 'word of the hidden/secret matter' — Foster 2005 renders 'a secret matter'; George 2003 'a hidden thing'; the lexeme *niṣirtu* can be 'secret', 'treasure', 'hidden thing'. The proem of the flood-narration sits here; the choice between *secret* and *hidden* affects the tonal register.
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.default_taken: a hidden matter (closer to Foster's *secret matter* while preserving the *niṣirtu*-as-hiddenness register)

editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.issue: *ana šakāni abūbi ublu libba-šunu ilānu rabûtu* 'to make a flood, the great gods' hearts inclined.' The verb *abālu* G 'to carry, bring' with *libbu* 'heart' as subject is the Akkadian idiom 'the heart drove them to'. Foster: 'the great gods' hearts were moved'; George: 'the great gods resolved'. Bidirectional with existing flood-decision glossary (`divine-decree-to-destroy-humankind-flood-trope-cross-corpus`); applied here.
options: the great gods' hearts were moved to bring on a flood
the great gods resolved to bring on a flood
the great gods' hearts inclined toward making a flood
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.default_taken: the great gods' hearts were moved to bring on a flood (Foster 2005)

editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.issue: *nin-šiku* — Ea's standing epithet, conventionally rendered 'Prince' (Foster) or 'wise prince' (George); the lexeme is a Sumerogram of disputed parsing.
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.default_taken: Prince (Foster 2005)

editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.issue: Boat-dimension *lū maš-lat rupšu-ša u mūrak-ša* 'let her breadth and her length be equal' — the cube-form construction. Translation register: should the literal 'equal' be retained, or should 'square' / 'cubic' be substituted for the modern reader? Bidirectional Gen 6:15 cross-corpus (the rectangular Hebrew ark vs. the cubic Babylonian boat) — major divergence-site.
options: let her breadth and her length be equal
let her be built as a cube
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.default_taken: let her breadth and her length be equal (preserves literal Akkadian without anachronistic geometry)
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.candidate_glossary_entry: Candidate: cube-vs-rectangular-flood-boat-cross-corpus (Babylonian cubic eleppu vs. Hebrew oblong tevah vs. Sumerian rounded ma-gur — three distinct hull-traditions for the flood vessel; named-scholarship George 2003, Finkel 2014 Ark Before Noah)

editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.issue: The famous double-meaning omen: *muḫrā kunūši ušaznan-kunūši nuḫša* 'upon you (the people) he will rain down abundance' — but *nuḫšu* 'abundance' is paired in the next verse with *kukkū* (vv46, 84, 87), which can mean either 'cakes' (= plenty) or 'darkness/disaster'. The equivocal omen is the diagnostic Mesopotamian Ea-doubletalk technique. Whether to flag the doubleness in English (e.g. parenthetical) or render only the surface-meaning (the audience-hearing) is an editorial decision.
options: render the equivocal sense in brackets or footnote
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.default_taken: surface-meaning only — the listener-on-the-spot hears abundance; the cosmic-reader knows otherwise; the doubleness is preserved structurally by Utnapishtim's reaction at v46+
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.candidate_glossary_entry: Candidate: kukku-darkness-cakes-equivocal-omen-cross-corpus (the famous Tablet XI doubletalk technique; cross-corpus to Greek oracle-doubletalk and Hebrew prophetic-ambiguity e.g. Jonah 3:4 *nehpāket*)

editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.issue: Cubit-measurement: *ikû iku-ša qaqqari kibri* 'her floor was one *ikû* (= field-measure); her sides one *kibru* each.' The *ikû* is a Mesopotamian field-measurement; George 2003 calculates ≈ 1 hectare or 60m sides. Should the English preserve the Akkadian unit, give a modern conversion, or both?
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.default_taken: preserve *ikû* untranslated with bracketed gloss '(= field-measure)' — scholarly convention
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.candidate_glossary_entry: Candidate: ikū-nindan-mesopotamian-flood-boat-dimension-units (the *ikû* and *nindan* unit-measurements at GILG-WOH-11:53-55; named-scholarship George 2003 510-518; cubical hull-form witness)

editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.issue: Seven-decks line *ur-tag-gi-ib-ši ana 6 lā* 'I gave her six decks (lit. roofed-her in six)' vs. v58 *ap-ta-ras-si ana 7* 'I divided her into 7'. Whether 6 deck-divisions or 7 internal compartments (or 6 + the keel = 7 total) is a recognized text-critical question (George 2003 510-518). Cross-corpus Gen 6:16 (Hebrew 3 decks) — major divergence.
options: six decks (= seven storeys counting the keel)
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.default_taken: six decks (v57) / seven (compartments) (v58) — preserves the literal Akkadian text-as-witnessed
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.candidate_glossary_entry: Candidate: seven-decks-vs-three-decks-flood-boat-multi-deck-cross-corpus (Babylonian 7-tier eleppu vs. Hebrew 3-tier tevah Gen 6:16; named-scholarship George 2003 510-518)

editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.issue: *kupru* 'pitch/bitumen' (written ESIR.UD.A) cross-corpus Gen 6:14 *kōper* 'pitch' — Akkadian/Hebrew direct Semitic cognates. Strong cross-corpus parallel; should it be flagged at glossary-level?
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.default_taken: bitumen — scholarly Assyriological convention; the Hebrew *kōper* cognate left for glossary-promotion review
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.candidate_glossary_entry: Candidate: kupru-koper-bitumen-pitch-flood-boat-waterproofing-cross-corpus (Akkadian *kupru* GILG-WOH-11:62-64 and Hebrew *kōper* Gen 6:14; direct Semitic-cognate flood-boat-waterproofing vocabulary; named-scholarship George 2003, Wenham 1987 WBC)

editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.issue: *akītu* — the Babylonian New Year festival, the supreme cultic-celebration of the Mesopotamian liturgical year. Should the term be preserved with gloss, transliterated only, or paraphrased ('the New Year festival')?
options: preserve *akītu* with bracket-gloss '(= New Year festival)'
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.default_taken: preserve *akītu* with bracket-gloss
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.candidate_glossary_entry: Candidate: akitu-new-year-festival-babylonian-supreme-cultic-celebration (the *akītu* simile at GILG-WOH-11:71; named-scholarship Cohen 1993 The Cultic Calendars of the Ancient Near East)

editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.issue: *būl ṣēri umām ṣēri mārī ummâni kalī-šunu uštēli* 'the cattle of the field, the wild beasts of the field, all the craftsmen — I brought up.' The craftsmen (*mārī ummâni* lit. 'sons of the craftsman') loading is unique to the Mesopotamian tradition (absent from the Hebrew ark). Major cross-corpus divergence; cross-corpus to Gen 6-7 (Noah's family only).
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.default_taken: render 'all the craftsmen'
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.candidate_glossary_entry: Candidate: marū-ummāni-craftsmen-on-the-flood-boat-mesopotamian-only-cross-corpus (the craftsmen-loading at GILG-WOH-11:82 — preservation of antediluvian technical-knowledge through the flood; absent from Hebrew tradition; named-scholarship George 2003 514, Foster 2005 ad loc)

editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.issue: *pa-la-ḫa-an-ni-ma ana libbi eleppi e-ru-ub-ma e-te-di-il bābī* 'I was afraid — I entered the boat and sealed my doors.' In Gilgamesh XI Utnapishtim seals the door himself; cross-corpus Gen 7:16 *wa-yyisgōr YHWH baʿadô* 'YHWH shut him in' — YHWH closes Noah's door. Major theological divergence-site.
options: render literal: Utnapishtim seals the door himself
no editorial intervention required (the divergence is in the source)
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.default_taken: render literal — divergence preserved in the translation; the Gen 7:16 contrast is editor-commentary territory
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.candidate_glossary_entry: Candidate: door-of-the-ark-who-shuts-it-flood-survivor-vs-deity-cross-corpus (Utnapishtim self-seals XI:90 vs. YHWH-shuts-Noah-in Gen 7:16; named-scholarship Heidel 1946, Wenham 1987 WBC)

editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.issue: Puzur-Amurri — the named boatman/pilot. Theophoric: *puzur* 'secret' + *Amurri* (the West-Semitic deity Amurru). Whether to gloss the name etymologically ('Secret-of-Amurru') or leave it as a proper-name.
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.default_taken: leave as proper-name — Puzur-Amurri
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.candidate_glossary_entry: Candidate: puzur-amurri-named-boatman-flood-pilot-cross-corpus (Tablet XI:92; cross-corpus Sumerian Flood Story unnamed-boatman; named-scholarship George 2003 514)

editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.issue: Adad's manifestation — Adad is the Mesopotamian storm-god (cross-corpus Hadad in West-Semitic; Baal-Hadad in Ugaritic). The cross-corpus reach is substantial; how much should it surface in the translation register vs. left for glossary-promotion?
options: render 'Adad' with brief cross-corpus gloss '(the storm-god; cf. Hadad)'
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.default_taken: render 'Adad' with no gloss — preserve as Akkadian divine-name; cross-corpus glossary-promotion pending
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.candidate_glossary_entry: Candidate: adad-hadad-baal-storm-god-cross-corpus-akkadian-ugaritic-hebrew-bible (Adad XI:96, 103; Hadad/Baal Ugaritic; Ps 29 YHWH-as-storm-god typology; named-scholarship Smith 2002 Origins of Biblical Monotheism, Day 1985 God's Conflict)

editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.issue: Shullat and Hanish — the twin-storm-heralds of Adad. Lesser-known divinities; whether to gloss them as 'storm-heralds' or leave unglossed.
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.default_taken: leave as proper-names

editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.issue: Errakal — a Nergal-aspect (death/pestilence god). *tarkullū* 'mooring-poles' that hold the cosmos in place — cosmographic image. Whether to gloss or render literally.
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.default_taken: leave as proper-name

editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.issue: *Anunnaki* — the chthonic council-of-gods. MAJOR LENS-RISK SITE: the magnet-term for popular-fringe ET-civilization readings (Sitchin and successors). WoH established acknowledgment-without-endorsement framework. Translation register: preserve the Akkadian form; gloss only philologically.
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.default_taken: preserve 'the Anunnaki' (the Anunnaki) — Akkadian divine-collective preserved; lens-discipline anchored at glossary level
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.candidate_glossary_entry: Candidate: anunnaki-akkadian-chthonic-council-gods-lens-risk-cross-corpus (Anunnaki XI:101, 122; cross-corpus Sumerian Anuna; LENS-RISK: WoH acknowledgment-without-endorsement framework; named-scholarship Black-Green 1992 Gods Demons and Symbols, Foster 2005)

editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.issue: *kašūšu* — the divine annihilation-instrument/disaster-weapon. The lexeme is a strong cosmic-cataclysm marker; whether to render 'cataclysm', 'disaster-weapon', 'destruction'.
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.default_taken: the cataclysm

editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.issue: The famous gods-curled-like-dogs simile: *ilānu kīma kalbi kunnunu ina kamāti rabṣu*. Foster 2005 'the gods cowered like dogs, crouching against the (outer) wall'; George 2003 'the gods were cowering like dogs, crouching by the outer wall'. The image is theologically humbling: the gods reduced to fearful animals. Foundational literary moment; default rendering should preserve the dog-simile literally.
options: the gods cowered like dogs, crouching against the outer wall
the gods were curled up like dogs at the outer wall
the gods, like dogs, lay coiled at the wall
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.default_taken: the gods cowered like dogs, crouching against the outer wall
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.candidate_glossary_entry: Candidate: ilānu-kīma-kalbi-gods-cower-like-dogs-flood-simile-cross-corpus (Tablet XI:113 — the gods reduced to fearful animals at the cosmic-wall; cross-corpus Sumerian Flood Story gods-weep; named-scholarship Foster 2005, George 2003)

editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.issue: *i-šas-si Ištar kīma ālitti* 'Ishtar cried out like a woman in childbirth.' The simile of cosmic-anguish. Foster 'screamed like a woman in childbirth'; George 'shrieked like a woman in labour'. Standard birth-simile vocabulary.
options: Ishtar cried out like a woman in childbirth
Ishtar screamed like a woman in labour
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.default_taken: Ishtar cried out like a woman in childbirth

editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.issue: *6 ūmī u 7 mušâti* 'six days and seven nights' — the famous Babylonian flood-duration. Cross-corpus Gen 7:12 (40 days + 40 nights) and Sumerian Flood Story (7 days + 7 nights). NOTABLE DIVERGENCE Gen-vs-Babylonian. Bidirectional existing glossary `seven-day-flood-vs-forty-day-flood-duration-tradition-cross-corpus` applied.
options: (it was) six days and seven nights
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.default_taken: for six days and seven nights

editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.issue: *imḫullu abūbu ik-la* 'the evil-wind, the flood, ceased.' *imḫullu* is the destructive cosmic-wind (cf. Enuma Elish IV; Marduk's seven winds). Existing central entry `im-hul-imhullu-destructive-storm-wind-mesopotamian-storm-vocabulary-cross-corpus` likely applies but the *appliesTo* list in glossary v2.64.0 does not include GILG-WOH refIds. Editor decision: extend appliesTo to GILG-WOH-11:130.
options: 'the destructive storm and the flood ceased'
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.default_taken: the evil-wind, the flood, ceased — preserves *imḫullu* as 'evil-wind' (standard rendering)
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.candidate_glossary_entry: Candidate: extend existing `im-hul-imhullu-destructive-storm-wind-mesopotamian-storm-vocabulary-cross-corpus` appliesTo to include GILG-WOH-11:130

editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.issue: *KUR Nimuš* 'Mount Nimush' — George 2003 reading; older Thompson 1930 / Heidel 1946 reads 'Mount Niṣir'. The sign-reading is now settled in favor of Nimush per George 2003's apparatus. Cross-corpus Gen 8:4 *hārê Ararat* 'mountains of Ararat' and Qur'an 11:44 *al-Jūdī* — three distinct mountain-landing traditions. MAJOR cross-corpus site. Existing glossary entry `harei-ararat` (Hebrew side) is bidirectional candidate.
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.default_taken: Mount Nimush — George 2003 critical-edition reading; Niṣir flagged in the editorial-question apparatus
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.candidate_glossary_entry: Candidate: mount-nimush-nisir-ararat-judi-flood-boat-landing-cross-corpus (Mount Nimush GILG-WOH-11:138; cross-corpus Mt Ararat Gen 8:4; al-Jūdī Q 11:44; three distinct mountain-traditions; named-scholarship George 2003, Westermann 1984, Wenham 1987 WBC)

editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.issue: Bird-test sequence: dove → swallow → raven (vv144-152). Cross-corpus Gen 8:6-12 has raven first, then three doves — INVERSE-ORDER. MAJOR cross-corpus divergence; the bird-test itself is one of the strongest cross-corpus narrative-parallels. Foster 2005, George 2003 preserve the Babylonian order literally.
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.default_taken: render literal — the dove → swallow → raven order is preserved; the Gen-divergence is editor-commentary territory
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.candidate_glossary_entry: Candidate: bird-test-dove-swallow-raven-flood-survival-test-cross-corpus (Tablet XI:144-152 dove-swallow-raven vs. Gen 8:6-12 raven-dove-dove-dove; cross-corpus Berossus dove-tradition; named-scholarship George 2003 516-519, Heidel 1946, Wenham 1987 WBC)

editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.issue: *aš-kun sur-qe-nu eli zikkurati ša šadî* 'I set up an incense-offering upon the *zikkurratu* of the mountain.' The cult-architecture term *ziqqurratu* applied here to a natural mountain-peak as natural-temple. *surqennu* 'incense-offering' — cult-vocabulary.
options: set up an incense-offering upon the ziggurat of the mountain
set up an offering on the mountain-peak
set up *surqennu* on the *ziqqurratu* of the mountain
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.default_taken: set up an incense-offering upon the ziggurat of the mountain — preserves both terms

editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.issue: *7 u 7 adagurrī* 'seven and seven cult-vessels' — the fourteen-vessel formula. *adagurru* is a clay cult-vessel for libations. Cross-corpus Gen 7:2 (seven pairs of clean animals). Sacred-seven-and-seven Hebrew tradition.
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.default_taken: seven and seven cult-vessels (*adagurrū*)

editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.issue: *ilānu i-ṣi-nu erīšu (ṭāba)* 'the gods smelled the (sweet) fragrance.' Cross-corpus Gen 8:21 *wa-yarach YHWH et reach ha-nichoach* 'YHWH smelled the pleasing aroma' — DIRECT lexical and semantic parallel; among the strongest Mesopotamian-Hebrew cross-corpus parallels. Existing central glossary `post-flood-thanksgiving-sacrifice-trope-cross-corpus` and `reach-hannichoach` (Hebrew side) are bidirectional.
options: the gods smelled the sweet savor
the gods smelled the pleasing aroma
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.default_taken: the gods smelled the sweet savor (preserves the *ṭāba* 'sweet/pleasing' across both vv157-158; closely parallels Hebrew *reach ha-nichoach*)

editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.issue: *ilānu kīma zumbī eli bēl niqê iptaḫru* 'the gods gathered like flies around the sacrificer.' The famous gods-like-flies simile — the post-flood gods are FAMISHED. CRITICAL CROSS-CORPUS DIVERGENCE: Gen 8:21 (YHWH smells alone, no fly-simile) is the theological inversion. Atrahasis III v 30-35 has the same image.
options: the gods gathered like flies around the sacrificer
the gods crowded like flies around the lord of the offering
the gods, like flies, swarmed about the one offering sacrifice
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.default_taken: the gods gathered like flies around the sacrificer (preserves the literal *zumbī* 'flies' and the technical *bēl niqê* 'lord of the sacrifice/sacrificer')
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.candidate_glossary_entry: Candidate: ilānu-kīma-zumbī-gods-gather-like-flies-divine-famine-cross-corpus (Tablet XI:159 / Atrahasis III v 30-35 — the post-flood divine-hunger image vs. Hebrew Gen 8:21 deity-decoupled-from-need; CRITICAL CROSS-CORPUS DIVERGENCE; named-scholarship Heidel 1946, Lambert-Millard 1969, Foster 2005)

editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.issue: *ulli nimēqī rabûti ša Anum īpu-šu kī ṣubāti-ya* 'she lifted up the great lapis-lazuli (necklace) which Anu had made for me as a (love-)token.' The rainbow-memorial-equivalent: Ishtar's lapis-lazuli necklace functions in Tablet XI as Yahweh's rainbow functions in Gen 9:13. NOTABLE CROSS-CORPUS PARALLEL: a colorful-arc-shaped divine-object set in heaven as a post-flood covenantal-sign. The Babylonian rainbow = Ishtar's necklace.
options: the great lapis-lazuli (necklace) which Anu made for me
the great jewels of lapis-lazuli that Anu had crafted for me
the great lapis-lazuli ornaments Anu had wrought for my pleasure
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.default_taken: the great lapis-lazuli (necklace) which Anu made for me
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.candidate_glossary_entry: Candidate: ishtar-lapis-lazuli-rainbow-covenant-cross-corpus (Ishtar's lapis-necklace Tablet XI:161-163 = post-flood memorial vs. Yahweh's rainbow Gen 9:13-17; both are colorful-arc-shaped divine memorials of the flood; named-scholarship Heidel 1946, George 2003, Wenham 1987 WBC)

editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.issue: *Igigi* — the seven (or ten) great gods of heaven (contrast Anunnaki = chthonic gods). LENS-RISK FLAG (like Anunnaki). Translation register: preserve Akkadian form.
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.default_taken: the Igigi-gods
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.candidate_glossary_entry: Candidate: igigi-akkadian-heavenly-gods-lens-risk-cross-corpus (Igigi XI:170; cross-corpus contrast with Anunnaki; LENS-RISK: popular-fringe magnet-term; WoH acknowledgment-without-endorsement framework; named-scholarship Black-Green 1992 Gods Demons and Symbols)

editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.issue: *bēl ḫīṭīti emid ḫīṭa-šu / bēl gillati emid gillata-šu* 'lay the sin on the sinner; lay the trespass on the trespasser.' THE FAMOUS PROPORTIONALITY PRINCIPLE — one of the earliest extant divine-justice-as-proportionate articulations in ANE literature. Cross-corpus Ezek 18:20, Deut 24:16. Major theological site.
options: lay the sin on the sinner; lay the trespass on the trespasser
let the offender bear his offense; let the transgressor bear his transgression
let punishment fall on the guilty; let trespass be borne by the trespasser
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.default_taken: lay the sin on the sinner; lay the trespass on the trespasser
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.candidate_glossary_entry: Candidate: bel-hititi-emid-hitasu-individual-responsibility-proportionate-justice-cross-corpus (Tablet XI:181-182; cross-corpus Ezek 18:20, Deut 24:16; foundational ANE individual-responsibility articulation; named-scholarship George 2003, Foster 2005, Greenberg 1980 on Ezek 18)

editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.issue: *Atra-ḫasīs šunatti ušabri-šum-ma piriš-ti ilī išmē* 'to Atrahasis I caused a dream to appear, and the secret of the gods he heard.' Utnapishtim called by his alternate name *Atra-ḫasīs* ('Surpassingly Wise'). Cross-corpus to the Atrahasis Akkadian flood-epic. Bidirectional existing glossary `ziusudra-atrahasis-utnapishtim-noach-flood-survivor-name-cluster-cross-corpus` applied here.
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.default_taken: Atra-ḫasīs (preserves the Akkadian form; scholarly convention)

editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.issue: *Ūta-napišti u sinništu-šu lū emû kī ilāni nāši* 'Utnapishtim and his wife shall become like us, the gods!' THE FAMOUS DEIFICATION line. Cross-corpus Gen 3:22 'the human has become like one of us' (the divine recognition-of-godlike-status) — but in Gen this causes expulsion; in Gilgamesh it is the REWARD. MAJOR cross-corpus contrast with Adapa lost-immortality. Bidirectional existing glossaries `til-digir-gin-kima-ilani-apotheosis-of-flood-survivor-cross-corpus` and `nemequ-napishtu-dariti-wisdom-but-not-immortality-paradigm-sage-cross-corpus` applied.
options: shall become like us, the gods
let them become like us, the gods
shall be (made) like the gods, like us
editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.default_taken: shall become like us, the gods

editorial_questions_resolved_in_editor_p.issue: *pī nārāti* 'mouth of the rivers' — the COSMIC PERIPHERY where the deified Utnapishtim is settled. Cross-corpus the Hebrew Eden-as-river-source (Gen 2:10-14, four rivers); Greek Hesperides; islands-of-the-blest.
options: at the mouth of the rivers
